title: Quicklaunch mockups for Hosted API: model cards, inline request builder & code presets
creator: Ava Patel
description: Deliver a fresh set of high-fidelity mockups and annotated screenshots for the Hosted API 'Quicklaunch' onboarding flow. This ticket covers three related screens: (1) a horizontally scrollable model-card picker that surfaces performance/cost badges and a quick-compare tooltip, (2) an inline 'request builder' panel that lets users craft a request with presets (completion, chat, embeddings) and advanced toggles (temperature, stop sequences, streaming), and (3) a code-snippet rail showing language presets (curl, Node.js, Python, Go) with copy-to-clipboard affordances. The deliverables are screenshot-ready frames in both light and dark themes, desktop/tablet/mobile breakpoints, and annotated assets for docs teams. Aim for concise copy and clear accessibility hints (aria labels, focus states) so engineering can implement without re-asking for wording or microcopy.
screenshots_spec: Export PNGs at 2x (desktop: 1440x900, tablet: 1024x768, mobile: 375x812). Include a 32px margin for doc headers. Annotated layers: callouts for badges (latency/cost), tooltip copy, keyboard focus ring, streaming indicator, and code copy button state. Provide both light and dark variants and a monochrome fallback for internal docs that display in grayscale.
acceptance_criteria: All three frame groups exported in figma and PNGs added to assets path
Annotations included as callout overlays (not flattened) in figma for engineering and docs
Code snippets have copyable text blocks exported to the repo (plaintext in PR) and match real API params used by ENG-9921
Accessibility notes (aria labels, keyboard flows) attached to each frame's description
PM signoff from Mara Jensen recorded in comments
design_notes: Key tradeoffs: compact model cards vs. detailed list. We chose compact horizontal cards because they allow scanning of important tradeoffs (latency/cost/quality badge) while preserving space for the inline request builder. Tooltip shows 2-line summary + 'compare' quick link to explorer. Request builder supports presets to reduce cognitive load: 'Default completion', 'Chat (system + messages)', 'Embeddings (text -> vector)'. Streaming UI uses a pulsing dot + 'Live' label to indicate incremental tokens. Code rail shows language toggles; snippets use the new SDK param names (model, temperature, max_tokens, stream=true). For the Go snippet we show the recommended client usage pattern implemented by ENG runtime team. Keep microcopy minimal and avoid jargon in the first-run experience.
